subject: Triangle connectivity assessment: VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S tradeoffs for OnPrem gateway
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@acumenbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Singhal <rajiv@edgeops.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: how should we link our on-prem gateway to Redwood Private?

Kimberly —

Thanks for the intro call today. Our security and infra teams asked for a short write-up that contrasts three onramp options so we can brief procurement and get a PO in flight: VPC peering, PrivateLink / interface endpoints, and a site-to-site (S2S) VPN. High-level constraints from our side:

- Must avoid public internet egress for inference traffic (data residency and compliance).
- Some inference workloads are latency-sensitive (sub-50ms p50 inside region).
- We have multiple AWS accounts across prod/us-east-1 and prod/eu-west-1.
- Network team prefers least operational burden but will accept an initial engineering investment.

Can you send a concise tradeoff summary and any config examples or templates? We also want to understand expected cost drivers (data transfer and extra infra).

Thanks —
Anna Lopez
Director, Cloud Platforms
Acumen Bank

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@acumenbank.com>, Rajiv Singhal <rajiv@edgeops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: how should we link our on-prem gateway to Redwood Private?

Anna / Rajiv —

Thanks — sketched the quick comparison below and attached a simple decision matrix and diagram. I tried to keep it short so your execs can scan it. TL;DR recommendation at the top, details after.

TL;DR recommendation: hybrid-first approach
- Use PrivateLink (interface endpoint) for control-plane and small-volume, compliance-sensitive paths (model control, key management endpoints).
- Use VPC peering between accounts/regions where low-latency, high-throughput inference is required and both sides are in the same cloud provider and account boundaries allow it.
- Use S2S VPN as a fallback for air-gapped sites, legacy network zones, or when PrivateLink cannot be supported by the customer network stack.

Why this mix?
- PrivateLink gives endpoint-level E2E (AWS-managed) connectivity and avoids exposure to public IPs; it is simpler for strict compliance because traffic stays inside the cloud provider's network and you can lock down access with security groups. Cost: charged per-hour/per-interface + data-processing fees; manageable for control-plane and low-volume traffic.
- VPC peering is cheapest per-byte for large volumes and lowest-latency inside a region but is limited by cross-account/transitive peering issues and doesn’t work across providers. It also requires careful route table management and can be operationally fiddly at scale across many accounts.
- S2S VPN is the most flexible (works for on-prem & multi-cloud) but introduces variable latency and maintenance overhead (tunnels, rekeys, MTU, route convergence). It can be adequate for non-latency-critical workloads or as a DR/fallback.

Key technical notes (short):
- Transitive limitations: VPC peering is non-transitive. If you have a hub-spoke model, PrivateLink or Transit Gateway are better fits.
- Path MTU and fragmentation: with S2S you must tune MTU to avoid fragmentation for jumbo inference payloads; tests showed up to 10-15% latency variance on heavy payloads with default MTU.
- Observability: each pattern requires different metrics. PrivateLink gives clean interface metrics; peering requires VPC flow logs and per-host telemetry; S2S needs VPN monitoring + BGP health where applicable.
- Autoscaling / ephemeral ENIs: Privatelink + our runtime works with endpoint ENIs; if the customer uses aggressive autoscaling we recommend sticky placement for inference nodes to avoid frequent ENI churn.

Cost drivers (what to expect):
- PrivateLink: hourly per-interface, per-GB processing fee. Good when volume is modest and compliance is required.
- VPC peering: mostly data transfer charges (intra-AZ often free, cross-AZ and cross-region billed). Best for high throughput inside same provider.
- S2S VPN: charges for active tunnels (hourly) + data transfer; if using hardware VPN appliances on-prem, factor in maintenance/HA redundancy.

Suggested next steps:
1) Run a quick traffic-profile capture over a 48h window to estimate byte volumes and latency targets (we can share a small collector script).
2) If volume is high and accounts are within the same cloud, prioritize VPC peering for compute plane and PrivateLink for control plane.
3) If you need single IP allowlisting and tighter compliance guarantees, do PrivateLink-first and use peering where permitted for bulk transfer.

Attached: connectivity-matrix.xlsx (simple decision table), network-diagram.png (recommended layout), s2s-config-snippets.txt (example tunnel).

Happy to jump on a 30m review tomorrow afternoon — propose 14:00 PT?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Quick addition from infra POV — agree with Kim's hybrid path. A few practical ops points to call out so Acumen can budget runbook and infra: 

- PrivateLink for control-plane: we should request a cross-account interface endpoint policy and recommend using security group restrictions. This makes allowlisting simple for your security team.
- Peering scale: if you plan >8 accounts peered to a single Redwood VPC, operational overhead becomes real (route table explosion). In that case, propose Transit Gateway or an edge NATing layer we host.
- Failover: recommend active-active with BGP (where supported) or two parallel tunnels for S2S. Tests show ~30-45s failover on standard IPSec rekey without BGP.

Action item for us: I can draft a short runbook (checklist + CLI snippets) for Peering and PrivateLink that covers VPC route hygiene, SG policies, and tag conventions.

—Ben

Subject: Re: Triangle connectivity assessment: VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S tradeoffs for OnPrem gateway

Adding some numbers from our pilot runs (sanitized):

- Measured per-token overhead: PrivateLink adds ~2-4ms p50 on top of baseline for small control calls; VPC peering p50 is +1ms inside same AZ.
- Data egress delta: for 10TB/mo, PrivateLink processing fees are roughly 8-12% of equivalent VPC peering transfer costs (varies by provider & region).
- VPN variance: standard S2S tunnels showed 10–60ms extra tail latency and jitter under load; not ideal for strictly latency-bounded inference.

Recommendation refinement:
- If Acumen's latency SLA requires <=50ms p50 end-to-end, measure the component of gateway-to-inference runtime inside your control; if it's minimal, PrivateLink is acceptable. If your runtime contributes >20ms, favor peering for the hot path.

Next steps I can own:
- Produce a short cost estimate using your expected monthly bytes (if you share the 48h capture).
- Draft a Transit Gateway fallback plan if you prefer hub-spoke over many peering links.

If everyone is aligned I’ll create the cost worksheet by EOD Wednesday.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior PM, Product Infra
Redwood Inference
